import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 5.1

by V. V. Belyaev, N. F. Sesekin

Is every locally finite minimal non-$FC$ group distinct from its derived
subgroup? The question has an affirmative answer for minimal non-$BFC$
groups.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«5.1»

variable {G : Type*} [Group G]

/-- The conjugacy class of an element $x$ in a group $G$. -/
def conjugacyClass (x : G) : Set G :=
  {y | IsConj x y}

/-- A group is locally finite if each of its finitely generated subgroups is finite. -/
def IsLocallyFiniteGroup (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.FG → (H : Set G).Finite

/-- An $FC$ group is a group in which every conjugacy class is finite. -/
def IsFCGroup (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ x : G, (conjugacyClass x).Finite

/-- A $BFC$ group is a group whose conjugacy classes have uniformly bounded finite size. -/
def IsBFCGroup (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ n : ℕ, ∀ x : G,
    (conjugacyClass x).Finite ∧ (conjugacyClass x).ncard ≤ n

/-- A minimal non-$FC$ group is not an $FC$ group, but all its proper subgroups are. -/
def IsMinimalNonFCGroup (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ¬ IsFCGroup G ∧ ∀ H : Subgroup G, H ≠ ⊤ → IsFCGroup H

/-- A minimal non-$BFC$ group is not a $BFC$ group, but all its proper subgroups are. -/
def IsMinimalNonBFCGroup (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ¬ IsBFCGroup G ∧ ∀ H : Subgroup G, H ≠ ⊤ → IsBFCGroup H

/--
Is every locally finite minimal non-$FC$ group distinct from its derived subgroup?
In other words, must every group $G$ that is locally finite, is not an $FC$ group,
and has only $FC$ proper subgroups satisfy $[G,G] \ne G$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem parts.b : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G],
      IsLocallyFiniteGroup G → IsMinimalNonFCGroup G → commutator G ≠ ⊤ := by
  sorry

/--
The corresponding question has an affirmative answer for minimal non-$BFC$ groups:
every locally finite group $G$ that is not a $BFC$ group and whose proper subgroups
are all $BFC$ groups satisfies $[G,G] \ne G$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 20]
theorem parts.b.variants.bfc : answer(True) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G],
      IsLocallyFiniteGroup G → IsMinimalNonBFCGroup G → commutator G ≠ ⊤ := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«5.1»

def IsFCGroup : Prop :=
  ∀ g : G, (conjugatesOf g).Finite

/-- A group $G$ is a $BFC$-group if there is a uniform bound on the number of conjugates
of its elements, i.e. there is some $n$ such that every conjugacy class of $G$ has at
most $n$ elements. -/
def IsBFCGroup : Prop :=
  ∃ n : ℕ, ∀ g : G, (conjugatesOf g).encard ≤ n

/-- A group $G$ is locally finite if every finitely generated subgroup of $G$ is finite. -/
def IsLocallyFinite : Prop :=
  ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.FG → Finite H

variable {G}

theorem IsBFCGroup.isFCGroup (h : IsBFCGroup G) : IsFCGroup G := by
  obtain ⟨n, hn⟩ := h
  exact fun g => Set.finite_of_encard_le_coe (hn g)

      simp [conjugatesOf, isConj_iff_eq, eq_comm]
    simp [this]⟩
